feedback_text: Could we add a dependency map between requirements? We often discover blockers after a sprint starts.
Please let us pin a decision owner and review date to each decision.
A Figma link preview inside a requirement would save our team several context switches.
I want reusable templates that prompt for edge cases, analytics, and rollout plans.
Can we see who changed acceptance criteria and when?
It would help to turn acceptance criteria into a checklist for testing.
Please add bulk editing for tags and owners.
A roadmap view grouped by outcome rather than release date would help explain priorities.
Could we get Slack alerts only for changes to decisions I follow?
Let us attach success metrics and show the latest measurement beside the hypothesis.
I need to link a requirement to an API spec and flag when that spec changes.
A sign-off step for regulated requirements would make approvals easier to audit.
Please support inline image annotations for mockup reviews.
An offline draft mode would help when reviewing specs during travel.
Could we compare two versions of a requirement side by side?
Saved filters for requirements missing testable criteria would catch gaps.
We need to export a project decision log as a clean PDF or CSV.
Please add rollout and rollback fields; those details get buried in comments.
A dashboard of stale requirements and pending reviews would help weekly check-ins.
Could RocketShip link requirements to GitHub pull requests and show implementation status?
I would like custom fields per workspace for different team needs.
Add project-level permissions for external reviewers.
A place to record rejected alternatives would preserve useful context.
Please let us flag ambiguous acceptance criteria and route them to the author.
A weekly digest of decisions made, changed, and still open would beat constant alerts.
Let me duplicate a feature with its checklist and links for similar work.
Could requirements support code snippets with readable formatting?
We need a lightweight intake form that non-product teams can submit.
Please add a simple way to embed prototypes without requiring public links.
A team directory synced to workspace ownership would reduce manual setup.
Let us attach test evidence to individual acceptance criteria.
I want to schedule a decision for review without creating a separate task.
A dependency warning when two features edit the same API would be useful.
Can we label assumptions separately from validated research?
A read-only share link with an expiry date would make reviews easier.
Please add markdown import so we can migrate existing specs.
Let users subscribe to a section instead of an entire project.
A small capacity note on roadmap items would help us avoid overcommitting.
Support multiple prototype links on one feature for responsive states.
Could archived decisions remain searchable from the current feature page?
The editor lags on long requirements, and typing falls behind.
Search misses terms unless I remember the exact project filter.
The comment panel leaves too little room to compare feedback with the spec.
Notifications are too noisy; I muted RocketShip after a few days.
It is hard to tell which acceptance criteria are current after a decision changes.
Exports lose headings and nested lists, so shared documents need cleanup.
There are too many clicks to create a decision from an existing requirement.
Editing anything beyond a short note on mobile is frustrating.
Permissions are confusing; I cannot quickly see who can edit a project.
The activity feed buries decisions among routine comments.
A workspace with hundreds of features takes long enough to load that I switch to a spreadsheet.
Link previews sometimes show stale page titles.
The default templates feel generic and take time to customize.
There is no clear distinction between target metrics and currently tracked metrics.
Keyboard shortcuts behave inconsistently across screens.
Archived projects still appear in search results.
It is easy to leave a requirement without an owner, and the product does not flag it.
The roadmap view gets cramped with many teams and milestones.
The audit trail does not explain why a permission changed.
I cannot quickly see what changed since my last review.
Pasting tables from a browser often breaks the formatting.
CSV import is brittle when columns are optional or headers differ slightly.
Decision owners do not get a useful reminder when a review date passes.
Comments look as prominent as the final approved decision.
Onboarding explains buttons but not how to structure a project.
The autosave indicator is subtle, so I am unsure whether my last change stuck.
Cross-project reporting requires too much manual exporting.
There is no obvious way to mark criteria blocked versus not tested.
The product shifts between “spec,” “feature,” and “requirement” across screens.
The browser tab title is generic when I have several projects open.
The permissions error does not say whether I need an owner or admin.
Overview charts cannot be downloaded for a planning deck.
The editor sometimes reorders numbered lists when I move a paragraph.
Review reminders ignore our working hours.
Filtering the decision log by author and date together is cumbersome.
Jira Product Discovery had flexible voting that we miss, though RocketShip keeps decisions with requirements.
Notion feels more forgiving for page editing; RocketShip makes structured specs easier.
Aha! has stronger roadmap visuals, while RocketShip preserves the reasoning behind choices.
Linear feels faster, but RocketShip gives decision history a proper home.
Coda made custom review flows easier; RocketShip is more focused.
Productboard aggregates feedback better; RocketShip is simpler for writing requirements.
Confluence cross-linked arbitrary pages more easily, but our old setup was messy.
Trello was quicker to scan; RocketShip captures decision context much better.
Airtable views were more customizable, while RocketShip has better decision records.
TestRail is clearer for test execution; RocketShip is where criteria should start.
Jira has more automation options, but RocketShip’s requirements are cleaner.
Figma comments are more natural for visuals; RocketShip makes decisions easier to preserve.
Google Docs was familiar, but RocketShip adds useful structure.
GitHub issues fit coding work better; RocketShip captures product rationale upstream.
Aha! reporting is more mature for executives; RocketShip is easier to keep current.
Notion wins for flexible internal docs, but RocketShip nudges us to record owners and decisions.
Linear notifications are easier to tune; RocketShip has better context.
Productboard tags customer feedback better; RocketShip turns choices into documented specs.
Confluence has more mature access controls in our setup; RocketShip is easier to navigate.
Trello made status obvious; I miss its simple board overview.
Airtable made custom reports easier; RocketShip’s built-in views are opinionated.
We still use TestRail for test cases; RocketShip needs a tighter handoff.
Jira Product Discovery was harder to learn, though its prioritization tools were stronger.
Miro is better for workshops; RocketShip preserves the decisions that come out of them.
Google Docs comments are faster; RocketShip gives us better traceability.
